dependencies.name: SQLite (better-sqlite3)
dependencies.rationale: better-sqlite3 is a synchronous SQLite binding. In-memory mode (:memory:) provides a real DB with no setup. Use real DB to catch SQL syntax errors and constraint violations that mocks would miss. Failure modes: locked DB, disk full, schema drift — all observable with a real in-memory DB.

dependencies.name: bcrypt
dependencies.rationale: bcrypt hashing is the security boundary. Mocking would defeat the test. Use a low cost factor (4) in tests for speed; production uses default (10).

dependencies.name: Express
dependencies.rationale: Use supertest to spin up the actual Express app. Express itself is well-tested upstream; we test our route configuration.

dependencies.name: WebSocket (ws)
dependencies.rationale: Use a real ws client (Node ws library) to test WebSocket lifecycle. The CI explicitly tests this with `pytest -m websocket`.

dependencies.name: helmet (security headers)
dependencies.rationale: Verify helmet sets the expected security headers (X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, HSTS). Tested in CI's 'Validate security headers' step.

dependencies.name: express-rate-limit
dependencies.rationale: Verify rate limiting triggers 429 after N requests. Use a low limit in tests to trigger it quickly.

dependencies.name: CORS
dependencies.rationale: Verify CORS headers on cross-origin requests. Low risk because misconfiguration is detectable and reversible.

dependencies.name: DOMPurify + jsdom (markdown sanitization)
dependencies.rationale: XSS protection is a security boundary. Real DOMPurify is required — mocking would defeat the test. Test known XSS payloads (script tags, onerror handlers, javascript: URLs).

dependencies.name: marked (markdown parsing)
dependencies.rationale: Standard markdown parser. Test edge cases (malformed markdown, empty input, large input).

dependencies.name: File system (Node fs)
dependencies.rationale: Use a real tmp directory for the DB file. Mock the path module only if needed.

dependencies.name: Node built-in: crypto
dependencies.rationale: Node's crypto module is well-tested upstream. Use it directly to generate session tokens and HMAC signatures.

dependencies.name: Docker (deployment)
dependencies.rationale: CI builds the Docker image and runs E2E tests in a container. Validates Dockerfile and runtime behavior.
